intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EYA1 gene on chromosome 8q13.3. Rickard et al. (2001) found a large de novo deletion including the EYA1 gene region in a patient with OFC syndrome, and Estefanía et al. (2006) found a single-nucleotide splice site substitution in EYA1 in another patient.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EYA1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a large deletion that includes EYA1 and calls OFC syndrome a contiguous gene deletion syndrome. It does not say the deletion is heterozygous or describe it as a mutation in EYA1 itself.

checks.claim: The EYA1 gene is located on chromosome 8q13.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the EYA1 gene (localised to 8q13.3)
checks.explanation: The abstract places EYA1 at 8q13.3.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) found a large de novo deletion including the EYA1 gene region in a patient with OFC syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: has identified de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and surrounding region in two patients with complex phenotypes involving features of BOR syndrome. One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a de novo large deletion of the EYA1 region in the OFC patient.

checks.claim: Estefanía et al. (2006) found a single-nucleotide splice site substitution in EYA1 in a patient with OFC syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Otofaciocervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome, but has features in addition to those of BOR syndrome (Rickard et al., 2001). Estefanía et al. (2006) described OFC syndrome as having changes of the face and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in BOR syndrome. BOR syndrome includes developmental defects of branchial arch structures, the middle and/or inner ear, and the kidney.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome but has additional features beyond those of BOR syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to BOR syndrome, with clinical features in addition to those of BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: Estefanía et al. (2006) described OFC syndrome as having changes of the face and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in BOR syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: OFC is characterized by trophic alterations of the facies and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in BOR.
checks.explanation: 'Changes of the face and shoulder girdle' restates 'trophic alterations of the facies and shoulder girdle'.

checks.claim: BOR syndrome includes developmental defects of branchial arch structures, the middle and/or inner ear, and the kidney.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal dominant disease that includes developmental defects of branchial arch structures, middle and/or inner ear and kidney.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Fára et al. (1967) reported familial otofaciocervical dysmorphia. According to Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995), features in this original family included lateral cervical fistulae.

checks.claim: Fára et al. (1967) reported familial otofaciocervical dysmorphia.
checks.evidence_quote: [Familial oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia].
checks.explanation: The title states that the paper reports familial oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: According to Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995), features in the original otofaciocervical family reported by Fára et al. (1967) included lateral cervical fistulae.
checks.evidence_quote: Some features present in the original family, including lateral cervical fistulae, have suggested that OFC syndrome could be a variant of BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the original family had lateral cervical fistulae. It does not name Fára et al. (1967), but it calls this family 'the original family'.

paragraphs.text: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a sporadic patient with OFC syndrome. Distinguishing features were a long face with a narrow nose, high-arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae, tetralogy of Fallot, and deafness caused by cochlear malformation. The patient did not have preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, or renal malformations. The authors noted that some features of the original family, including lateral cervical fistulae, had suggested that OFC syndrome might be a variant of BOR syndrome. However, they concluded that this patient's distinct facial and radiographic findings and markedly downward-sloping shoulders supported OFC syndrome as a unique, clinically recognizable entity.

paragraphs.text: Pohl et al. (2013) studied a large consanguineous Turkish family with autosomal recessive OFC syndrome. Features included facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits, hearing impairment, branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability. Whole-exome sequencing of a pooled DNA sample from 4 affected individuals identified a homozygous c.497G-T variant in the PAX1 gene, which resulted in a gly166-to-val (G166V) substitution within the paired-box domain. The variant cosegregated with the disease in the family. In a luciferase reporter assay in HEK293T cells, the corresponding mouse mutant Pax1 (G157V) showed significantly reduced transactivation of a regulatory sequence in the Nkx3-2 promoter compared with wildtype. This result suggested that the mutant protein had reduced DNA-binding affinity.

checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with OFCS from Turkey, we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES)

paragraphs.text: Rickard et al. (2001) developed a fluorescent quantitative multiplex PCR dosage assay for 3 of the 3-prime exons of the EYA1 gene (exons 7, 9, and 13) and combined it with microsatellite marker analysis. Using this approach, they found de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and the surrounding region in 2 patients with complex phenotypes that included features of BOR syndrome. One of these patients had OFC syndrome and carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region. The authors concluded that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome and is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome. They compared the boundaries of this deletion with other reported rearrangements of the region. This comparison narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome to an interval of about 1 cM between markers D8S553 and D8S1797.

checks.explanation: The assay and the three exons match the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: has identified de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and surrounding region in two patients with complex phenotypes involving features of BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.explanation: The markers and the roughly 1 cM interval match the abstract.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with OFC syndrome, Estefanía et al. (2006) identified a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of the EYA1 gene. They concluded that patients with OFC syndrome can carry point mutations that alter the EYA1 reading frame, as well as large rearrangements. This finding argued against the hypothesis that OFC syndrome is caused only by contiguous deletions of EYA1 and adjacent genes.

checks.evidence_quote: we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Estefanía et al. (2006) concluded that patients with OFC syndrome can carry point mutations that alter the EYA1 reading frame, as well as large rearrangements.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.
checks.explanation: This matches the abstract's stated conclusion.

checks.claim: The EYA1 splice site substitution found by Estefanía et al. (2006) argued against the hypothesis that OFC syndrome is caused only by contiguous deletions of EYA1 and adjacent genes.
checks.evidence_quote: led to the hypothesis that OFC is caused by contiguous deletions of EYA1 and adjacent genes. By contrast, we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1.
checks.explanation: The abstract presents the point-mutation finding as running against the contiguous-deletion hypothesis.
